name: X (Twitter)
summary: No approval queue, but every API call costs money: you buy pay-per-use credits in the X Developer Console before your agent can read or post.
scenario: An agent that reads a user's timeline and mentions and posts on their behalf.

composio.note: Check the Composio managed OAuth directory for the Twitter/X toolkit.

portal.accountNeeded: An X account and a payment card in the Developer Console.

policyAndDomain.detail: Callback URLs must match exactly; no policy verification described.

userCapBeforeApproval.detail: No user cap, but pay-per-use plans cap Post reads at 3 million per month.

appReview.detail: No approval step described; apps can be suspended with an appeal process.

paidOrPartner.detail: Pay-per-use credits (e.g. $0.005 per Post read, $0.015 per Post created). Commercial use at scale needs an Enterprise plan.

time.note: No review wait; budget and credits are the gate.

nextStep: Create an app in console.x.com, set up OAuth 2.0 user authentication (Web App, confidential client) with your exact callback URL, buy credits and set a spending limit.

prerequisites.text: A payment card and a spending limit for pay-per-use credits.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: In console.x.com click Create App and enter name, description and use case. Copy keys immediately; they're shown once.

steps.title: Set up OAuth 2.0 user authentication
steps.detail: Choose Web App (confidential client) and add callback URLs (max 10, exact match, https in production; use 127.0.0.1 not localhost locally).

steps.title: Implement PKCE and offline access
steps.detail: Use authorization code with PKCE and request offline.access, or tokens expire after 2 hours with no refresh token.

steps.title: Buy credits and set a cap
steps.detail: Purchase credits, set a per-cycle spending limit, and estimate cost per agent action.

review.summary: No approval queue. Cost is the main gate; apps can be suspended for policy violations.
review.meanwhile: Usable as soon as you have credits.

blockers.fix: You hit your spending limit or the 3M Post-read cap; raise the limit or move to Enterprise.
Request offline.access to get refresh tokens.

nuances.text: X replaced its $200/month entry plan with pay-per-use in 2026.
Posts that include a URL cost far more to create ($0.20) than plain posts.

uncertainties: Prices may change; X shows current rates in the Developer Console.

sources.title: X Docs: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE
Open Terms Archive: X replaces its $200 plan with pay-per-use

corrections: Expected the $200/month Basic tier. X moved to pay-per-use credits in 2026.
